subject: Recourse allocation & SLA credits — draft MSA redlines
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sally White <sally.white@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Recourse allocation & SLA credits — draft MSA redlines

Hi Sally / Acme team,

Following our call this morning, attaching a short note on the liability/credits tradeoff we discussed. We pulled together a compromise we think is operationally clear and preserves commercial protections for both sides. High level ask: legal to review language and confirm we can move forward to procurement with this compromise.

Key proposal (summary):
- Keep an overall contract liability cap (aggregate damages) tied to 12 months of fees.
- Exclude statutory liabilities (e.g., gross negligence, willful misconduct, personal injury) from that cap.
- For service availability claims, make service credits the "sole and exclusive" remedy, capped at the lesser of 6 months of fees or actual fees paid in the prior 12 months.
- Important: credits for availability would be excluded from the general liability cap (i.e., credits do not count toward the 12-month cap). For other damage categories, the 12-month cap applies as usual.

Rationale: This preserves a fast path for operational outages (credits only) which our ops teams can automate, while keeping liability exposure bounded for other sorts of claims. It also avoids double-counting (credits + damages) in catastrophic availability scenarios.

Attached: initial redline with the specific contract wording we propose (MSA_redline_mk_neha_20261118.docx).

Neha / Dev — can you review the attached and call out any legal/commercial concerns? Dev, if procurement needs a different cap or wants credits counted toward the cap, flag that now so we can evaluate.

Next step: if we have alignment, we'll ask Acme to accept this approach in the Order Form and we can send a DocuSign stub.

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Recourse allocation & SLA credits — draft MSA redlines

Marcus — thanks for laying this out. I reviewed and marked up the redline. High-level comments below and I put a tracked-change draft in the attachment.

1) Credits as sole remedy — I support making credits the exclusive remedy for service-availability claims, with a fixed cap. That helps operationalize outages and limits litigation risk.

2) Credits excluded from the liability cap — this point is the crux. Excluding credits from the general liability cap is defensible if the credits are genuinely prospective (i.e., they apply only to availability) and are narrowly drafted. We should:
   - Explicitly limit the credits to defined "Availability Events" in the SLA.
   - Exclude credits from the cap only to the extent they arise under the SLA (not for other breaches).
   - Add express carveouts for indirect/consequential damages (continue to exclude these broadly) and then make it explicit that statutory remedies (e.g., data protection fines) also survive.

3) Measurement window and stacking — propose limiting the credit cap to the "lesser of 6 months fees or fees paid in the prior 12 months" rather than 12 months to reduce exposure. If procurement pushes back, we can trade a lower credit cap for excluding credits from the cap.

4) Sole remedy language should have a survival clause and a mutual waiver of other remedies only for availability claims. We should also ensure indemnities for third-party IP/data claims remain outside these limits.

I've attached annotated language (MSA_redline_mk_neha_20261118.docx). Please consider the below draft bullet to include in the MSA: 

"Service Availability; Exclusive Remedy. For Availability Events as defined in the SLA, Customer's sole and exclusive remedy shall be service credits described in the SLA, capped at the lesser of six (6) months of fees paid in the prior twelve (12) month period or actual fees paid. Service credits issued under the SLA shall not be included in the calculation of the aggregate liability cap set forth in Section X. This exclusive remedy shall apply only to claims directly arising from Availability Events and shall not limit Customer's remedies for claims arising from willful misconduct, gross negligence, or statutory liabilities."
If that language is acceptable commercially, we can present it to Acme. Dev — if procurement needs credits counted toward the cap, what's the minimum commercial concession you can accept (e.g., increase overall cap to 18 months or lower credit cap to 3 months)?

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recourse allocation & SLA credits — draft MSA redlines

Marcus / Neha — thanks for circulating. Acme's initial feedback from legal/procurement is below. We're sympathetic to the desire to automate outage remediation, but we cannot accept credits being excluded from the overall liability cap as a general rule. Specific points: 

- Counting credits outside the cap effectively leaves a layer of uncapped exposure in large-scale downtime scenarios; our finance team will not sign off.
- Acme can accept credits as the sole remedy for Availability Events, but credits must be counted toward the aggregate liability cap (or alternatively, the cap must be increased substantially).
- We would consider excluding credits from the cap only for routine short interruptions (e.g., single-region blips under 4 hours) and not for multi-region outages or repeated failures.

I've attached Acme's redlines and comments (acme_comments_20261119.pdf). Can we set a short call to talk tradeoffs? Thursday morning our time works.

Best,
Sally White
Director, Procurement
Acme Corp

Subject: Final proposal: hybrid approach for credits and caps

Sally / Acme team — thanks for the quick feedback and for the call on Thursday. We discussed internally with Legal and Commercial and are proposing a compromise that we believe addresses Acme's budgetary concerns while keeping the operational benefit of credits. Proposed final language summary below; see attached clean draft MSA (MSA_proposal_v3.docx).

Proposed compromise (summary):
1) Aggregate liability cap: 12 months of fees (survival and statutory carveouts unchanged).
2) Service credits: Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for Availability Events shall be service credits as defined in the SLA. Service credits will be capped at the lesser of six (6) months of fees or fees paid in the prior 12 months.
3) Limited carve for routine incidents: Service credits arising from routine, single-region Availability Events (under four hours) shall be excluded from the aggregate liability cap.
4) Major incidents and repeated outages: Service credits arising from multi-region or repeated Availability Events (more than two events in a rolling 12-month period) shall be counted toward the aggregate liability cap.

Why this helps both sides:
- Acme gets assurance that systemic/major outages will be folded into the liability calculus (avoids uncapped catastrophic exposure).
- Redwood can operate predictable, automated crediting for routine incidents without constantly engaging legal.

Next steps:
- Neha: include the clean redline in the MSA with the definitions for "Availability Event", "routine incident", and the stacking/counting rules.
- Dev / Procurement: if Acme accepts, please confirm and we'll send DocuSign for the Order Form (link below).

Thanks,
